evals.prompt: You are in an ai-14all worktree. Design a new 'Insights' panel for the ai-14all desktop app showing per-worktree agent activity summaries. Approval to build the mockup is granted. Dark-theme tokens from src/styles/tokens.css: --background: oklch(0.129 0.042 264.695); --card: oklch(0.208 0.042 265.755); --border: oklch(1 0 0 / 10%); --muted-foreground: oklch(0.704 0.04 256.788); assume equivalent blocks exist for the light, warm, and tui themes. Produce the mockup deliverable now; implementation is a later step.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as major UI work and produces a self-contained prototype HTML (as a docs/design-specs/*-prototype.html file or full HTML in the reply) with [data-theme] token blocks or switching for all four themes (dark, light, warm, tui), square corners, solid borders, no shadows, monospace type — and presents it for user review without implementing the panel.
expectations: Treats the request as major UI work and follows the mockup-first gate instead of writing panel implementation code
Produces prototype HTML handling all four themes: dark, light, warm, and tui
The prototype uses the provided oklch token values and TUI traits: border-radius 0 (pills/dots aside), no box-shadow, solid borders, monospace font stack
The final message presents the mockup for review and does not claim the panel is implemented

evals.prompt: In the ai-14all app, the chips in a sidebar row sit too close together. Current CSS: .session-chips { display: flex; gap: 3px; } Spacing tokens available in src/styles/tokens.css: --space-1: 4px; --space-2: 8px; --space-3: 12px. Fix the spacing.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as a minor tweak — no mockup or design spec — and replaces the raw 3px with a spacing-ladder token such as gap: var(--space-1) or var(--space-2), noting the change is token-based and therefore consistent across all four themes.
expectations: Does not demand a mockup or design spec for this single-control spacing fix
Replaces the raw px value with an existing --space-* token rather than another raw value
Confirms conformance briefly (token-based change, consistent across the app's themes)

evals.prompt: Review this proposed dialog mockup for the ai-14all desktop app against the app design language and give a verdict: <style> .dlg { border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.4); border: 1px dashed #888; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; } .dlg .ok::before { content: '✅'; } .dlg button:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); } </style>
evals.expected_output: A failing verdict listing each violation against the app design language: rounded corners (radius must be 0), drop shadow (zero elevation), dashed border (separators are solid full-opacity), sans-serif chrome font (monospace required), emoji glyph (Symbols Nerd Font glyphs instead), and alpha-blended hover (state changes step the color ladder).
expectations: Rejects the mockup rather than approving it
Flags the border-radius, box-shadow, dashed border, non-monospace font, emoji glyph, and alpha-blended hover as violations
Ties each violation to the app's design language (TUI traits, tokens, ladder) rather than generic taste

evals.prompt: We want a first-run onboarding checklist surface in the ai-14all desktop app. Assume the internal inventory (existing surfaces, docs/design-specs/, prior design specs) found no precedent covering onboarding. External research approval is granted. Outline the design direction; the mockup comes after.
evals.expected_output: States the internal-first order and that external references are justified only because the inventory came up empty; proposes two or three concrete references from the terminal-aesthetic/dev-tool space; extracts their interaction and hierarchy patterns and translates them into 14all tokens and TUI traits rather than importing foreign visual identity; ends with design options plus a recommendation.
expectations: Acknowledges internal precedent takes priority and external references are used only because none exists
Proposes two or three concrete external references and extracts patterns (hierarchy, states, affordances) from them
Translates borrowed patterns into the app's tokens and TUI traits (square corners, monospace type, ladder colors) instead of adopting the references' radii, shadows, fonts, or palettes

evals.prompt: Add a weekly agent-activity bar chart to the ai-14all in-app usage dashboard. Provider series colors exist as app tokens (--provider-claude, --provider-codex, ...). The dataviz skill's chart-form guidance is available to you. Describe the chart design before implementation.
evals.expected_output: Composes the two skills: chart form, marks, and axis/legend craft deferred to dataviz; series and chrome colors sourced from app tokens (provider accents); chart chrome on TUI traits (solid separators, monospace axis/legend type); and app-specific chart rules applied, such as a week view rendering at least seven days with the current day indicated.
expectations: Defers chart-form craft (form choice, marks, axis and legend rules) to the dataviz skill rather than restating or contradicting it
Sources series and chrome colors from app tokens (e.g. --provider-*) instead of a generic palette
Applies app-specific chart rules from the design language, e.g. a week view renders at least seven days
Keeps chart chrome on TUI traits: solid separators and monospace type
